title: Next.js cookies() and headers(): Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on reading request data with cookies() and headers() in Server Components, Route Handlers and Server Actions, where cookies can be set, how they force dynamic rendering, and what the Edge and Node.js runtimes support.

chapters.title: cookies() and headers() Mental Model
points: cookies() and headers() are async functions from next/headers: use `const store = await cookies()`, since they return Promises in current Next.js
Both are request-time APIs: they read the incoming HTTP request, so they only work on the server (Server Components, Route Handlers, Server Actions, middleware/proxy), never in Client Components
headers() returns a read-only Web Headers object: `(await headers()).get('user-agent')`; header names are case-insensitive and you cannot set response headers through it
cookies() returns a store with get(name), getAll(), has(name), set(), delete(); get returns `{ name, value }` or undefined, so use `?.value`
Reading is allowed everywhere on the server, but writing cookies is restricted to Server Actions and Route Handlers

chapters.title: Where You Can Read and Set Cookies
points: Server Component: read only, calling cookies().set() throws an error because streaming means headers are already sent before the component renders
Why: a cookie is set through a Set-Cookie response header, and a Server Component renders after the response has started streaming
Server Action: can read, set and delete cookies, so use it for login, logout, theme or consent flows: `(await cookies()).set('session', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, path: '/' })`
Route Handler: can read and set cookies via cookies() or by returning `new Response(null, { headers: { 'Set-Cookie': '...' } })`
Delete with `store.delete('name')` or set with maxAge: 0; the path and domain must match the original cookie or it will not be removed

chapters.title: Dynamic Rendering Triggered by Request APIs
points: Calling cookies() or headers() opts the route into dynamic rendering: it renders per request instead of being prerendered at build time
Both are request-time APIs, so the whole route becomes dynamic, not only the component that calls them
Reading searchParams or params without generateStaticParams, and uncached fetches, are other dynamic triggers; with cacheComponents, request APIs must sit inside Suspense or the build errors
Isolate the dynamic part: wrap the component that reads cookies in `<Suspense fallback={...}>` so the rest of the page can stay static or be prerendered
Route Handlers: GET is dynamic only when it uses request APIs (cookies, headers, the Request object); otherwise it may be statically evaluated, depending on the Next.js version and config

chapters.title: Edge vs Node.js Runtime
points: Set per route with `export const runtime = 'edge'` or `'nodejs'`; Node.js is the default
Edge runs on V8 isolates with Web APIs only (fetch, Request, Response, Headers, crypto.subtle): fast cold start, global distribution, small bundle size limits
Node.js runtime supports the full Node API (fs, net, child_process, Buffer, native modules), most npm packages, and database drivers using TCP
cookies() and headers() work in both runtimes, since both expose the same Web-standard request and response objects

Edge cannot use fs, native addons or many ORMs and TCP database clients, and it does not support ISR or the Node-only features; choose Edge only for light logic like auth checks or redirects, otherwise stay on Node.js

chapters.title: Common Mistakes
points: Using cookies().get() without await: returns a Promise, so `.value` is undefined
Calling cookies().set() inside a Server Component or during render: throws; move it to a Server Action or Route Handler
Reading cookies in a layout or page by accident and silently turning the whole route dynamic, which loses static caching
Setting auth cookies without httpOnly, secure and sameSite flags, which exposes them to JavaScript and CSRF
Importing a Node-only module such as fs in a route marked runtime = 'edge', which fails the build

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet
points: Import: `import { cookies, headers } from 'next/headers'`; always `await` them
Read: `(await cookies()).get('x')?.value`, `(await headers()).get('x')`
Write cookies only in: Server Action, Route Handler (not Server Component or render)
Using either one = dynamic rendering for that route; wrap in Suspense to limit the dynamic part
Runtime: `export const runtime = 'edge' | 'nodejs'`; default nodejs; Edge = Web APIs only, Node = full Node API
